rows.stem: Find the cardinal number of the following sets.
rows.sourceEnglish: M = {p, q, r, s, t, u}

steps.reason: The cardinal number counts the distinct elements of a set.
steps.equation: M = {p, q, r, s, t, u}

steps.reason: List the elements once; none is repeated.
steps.equation: p, q, r, s, t, u

steps.reason: There are six elements, so the cardinal number is six.

rows.stem: Find the cardinal number of the following sets.
rows.sourceEnglish: P = {x : x = 3n+2, n∈W and x< 15}

steps.reason: Whole numbers start at zero; use x=3n+2 and the upper limit.
The allowed whole numbers are 0 through 4.
Substitute these five values and count the distinct results.

rows.stem: Find the cardinal number of the following sets.

steps.reason: The printed expression is four divided by the whole product 3n, not (4/3)n.
Natural numbers strictly above 2 and at most 5 are 3, 4, and 5.
Evaluate one fraction for each n and count the different values.

rows.stem: Find the cardinal number of the following sets.
rows.sourceEnglish: R = {x : x is an integers, x∈Z and −5 ≤ x < 5}

steps.reason: The lower endpoint −5 is included, but the upper endpoint 5 is excluded.
Write every integer in this interval.
Count from −5 through 4, inclusive.

rows.stem: Find the cardinal number of the following sets.
rows.sourceEnglish: S = The set of all leap years between 1882 and 1906.

steps.reason: Check multiples of four between the stated years.
A century year is a leap year only when divisible by 400. Exclude 1900.
Keep the five actual leap years and count them.

rows.stem: Identify the following sets as finite or infinite.
rows.sourceEnglish: X = The set of all districts in Tamilnadu.

steps.reason: A finite set has a limited number of members.
At any fixed time, a state has a finite list of districts; the list can change.
Hence X is a finite set.

rows.stem: Identify the following sets as finite or infinite.
rows.sourceEnglish: Y = The set of all straight lines passing through a point.

steps.reason: Fix one point in a plane.
Each different direction gives another straight line through P.
steps.equation: The number of possible directions is infinite

steps.reason: There is no limit to the number of distinct lines through P.

rows.stem: Identify the following sets as finite or infinite.
rows.sourceEnglish: A = {x : x∈Z and x < 5}

steps.reason: The condition includes every integer smaller than five.
There is no smallest negative integer; the list continues without end.
Therefore the set has infinitely many elements.

rows.stem: Identify the following sets as finite or infinite.

steps.reason: Factor the quadratic expression.
A product is zero when one factor is zero.
Both roots are natural numbers, and there are no others.

rows.stem: Which of the following sets are equivalent or unequal or equal sets?
rows.sourceEnglish: A = The set of vowels in the English alphabets. B = The set of all letters in the word “VOWEL”.

steps.reason: List the distinct letters in each set.
steps.equation: A = {a, e, i, o, u}; B = {V, O, W, E, L}

steps.reason: Each set has five elements, but the members differ.
Same number of members means the sets are equivalent.

rows.stem: Which of the following sets are equivalent or unequal or equal sets?

steps.reason: List the whole numbers strictly between 1 and 5.
Compare D with the given set C.
The element 5 is in C but not in D.

rows.stem: Which of the following sets are equivalent or unequal or equal sets?
rows.sourceEnglish: X = {x : x is a letter in the word “LIFE”} Y = {F, I, L, E}

steps.reason: Write the distinct letters appearing in LIFE.
Compare those members with Y; order does not matter in a set.
Both sets contain exactly the same four elements.

rows.stem: Which of the following sets are equivalent or unequal or equal sets?
rows.sourceEnglish: G = {x : x is a prime number and 3 < x < 23} H = {x : x is a divisor of 18}

steps.reason: List the primes strictly between 3 and 23.
List the positive divisors of 18.
Both sets contain six distinct members, but different values.

rows.stem: Identify the following sets as null set or singleton set.

steps.reason: There is no natural number strictly between consecutive integers 1 and 2.
So the membership condition has no solution.
A set without elements is called the null or empty set.

rows.stem: Identify the following sets as null set or singleton set.
rows.sourceEnglish: B = The set of all even natural numbers which are not divisible by 2

steps.reason: Every even natural number is divisible by two by definition.
The question requires an even number that is not divisible by two.
Thus B has no members.

rows.stem: Identify the following sets as null set or singleton set.

steps.reason: The curly brackets contain the number zero as one element.
This is not the empty set: it contains one element.
A one-element set is a singleton.

rows.stem: Identify the following sets as null set or singleton set.
rows.sourceEnglish: D = The set of all triangles having four sides.

steps.reason: By definition, every triangle has exactly three sides.
No triangle has four sides.
Therefore D is the null set.

rows.stem: State which pairs of sets are disjoint or overlapping?
rows.sourceEnglish: A = {f, i, a, s} and B = {a, n, f, h, s}

steps.reason: Find the letters appearing in both sets.
steps.equation: A = {f, i, a, s}; B = {a, n, f, h, s}

steps.reason: Their common elements are a, f, and s.
The intersection is nonempty, so the sets overlap.

rows.stem: State which pairs of sets are disjoint or overlapping?
rows.sourceEnglish: C = {x : x is a prime number, x > 2} and D = {x : x is an even prime number}

steps.reason: The only even prime number is two.
C contains only prime numbers greater than 2, so it excludes 2.
There is no common element.

rows.stem: State which pairs of sets are disjoint or overlapping?
rows.sourceEnglish: E = {x : x is a factor of 24} and F = {x : x is a multiple of 3, x < 30}

steps.reason: List the positive factors of 24.
List the positive multiples of 3 below 30.
The sets share 3, 6, 12, and 24.

rows.stem: If S = {square, rectangle, circle, rhombus, triangle}, list the elements of the following subset of S.
rows.sourceEnglish: The set of shapes which have 4 equal sides.

steps.reason: Look for figures with four sides of equal length.
steps.equation: square: 4 equal sides; rhombus: 4 equal sides

steps.reason: A general rectangle does not necessarily have four equal sides.
Choose the square and rhombus from S.

rows.stem: If S = {square, rectangle, circle, rhombus, triangle}, list the elements of the following subset of S.
rows.sourceEnglish: The set of shapes which have radius.

steps.reason: Radius is the distance from the centre of a circle to its boundary.
steps.equation: r = distance from centre to circle

steps.reason: Among the shapes listed in S, the circle is the one identified by a radius.
The requested subset contains one element.

rows.stem: If S = {square, rectangle, circle, rhombus, triangle}, list the elements of the following subset of S.
rows.sourceEnglish: The set of shapes in which the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

steps.reason: A triangle has three interior angles that total 180 degrees.
Quadrilaterals in S have an interior-angle sum of 360 degrees.
Only a triangle has the requested total.

rows.stem: If S = {square, rectangle, circle, rhombus, triangle}, list the elements of the following subset of S.
rows.sourceEnglish: The set of shapes which have 5 sides.

steps.reason: A five-sided polygon is called a pentagon.
S contains a circle, triangle, and three four-sided shapes, not a pentagon.
No listed element qualifies.

rows.stem: If A = {a, {a, b}}, write all the subsets of A.

steps.reason: The outer set A has two elements: a and the inner set {a,b}.
A two-element set has four subsets.
List the empty set, both singleton subsets and A itself.

rows.stem: Write down the power set of the following sets:
rows.sourceEnglish: A = {a, b}

steps.reason: A contains two distinct elements.
Choose no elements, each singleton, or both.
Write these four subsets together as a power set.

rows.stem: Write down the power set of the following sets:

steps.reason: Three distinct members have two choices each: include or omit.
Group the subsets by size zero, one, two and three.
List all eight subsets without repetition.

rows.stem: Write down the power set of the following sets:
rows.sourceEnglish: D = {p, q, r, s}

steps.reason: Four distinct members give 2^4 subsets.
Take all subsets with zero or one element.
Add the six two-element subsets.
Add the four triples and the full set.
The complete power set is precisely the sixteen subsets listed above.

rows.stem: Write down the power set of the following sets:

steps.reason: The set E has no elements.
Every set has the empty set as a subset, including E itself.
There is no other subset of an empty set.

rows.stem: Find the number of subsets and the number of proper subsets of the following sets.
rows.sourceEnglish: W = {red, blue, yellow}

steps.reason: The set has three distinct colours.
Each element can be included or excluded from a subset.
Exclude W itself when counting proper subsets.

rows.stem: Find the number of subsets and the number of proper subsets of the following sets.
rows.sourceEnglish: X = {x² : x∈N, x² ≤ 100}

steps.reason: The allowed natural numbers are 1 through 10.
Their squares are ten distinct elements of X.
Calculate all subsets using 2 raised to the cardinal number.
Exclude X itself for proper subsets.

rows.sourceEnglish: If n(A) = 4, find n[P(A)].

steps.reason: An n-element set has 2^n subsets.
Substitute n(A)=4.
Evaluate.

rows.sourceEnglish: If n(A) = 0, find n[P(A)].

steps.reason: Even an empty set has one subset, the empty set.
Apply the power-set cardinality rule.
Evaluate.

rows.sourceEnglish: If n[P(A)] = 256, find n(A).

steps.reason: Write the power-set count as a power of two.
Recognise 256 as two to the eighth power.
The exponents must match.
